eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from Météo-France and other models indicate a cooling trend for Paris on May 31 following a mid-week heat dome that drove highs near 33–34°C. A frontal passage and lingering moisture are expected to moderate temperatures into the low- to mid-20s Celsius range, with isolated showers possible that limit peak heating. Ensemble guidance shows tight clustering around 23–25°C maxima, consistent with climatological May averages near 20–21°C yet tempered by the post-heatwave setup. Traders price 23°C highest at 31.5% as the most probable outcome under current model consensus, while slight spreads in steering winds or timing of cloud cover could shift the daily high by 1–2°C. Updated model runs and official briefings through the weekend will refine resolution thresholds.

eventMetadata.context_description: Short-range forecasts from INMET and global models place São Paulo’s May 31 maximum near 22–24 °C under building high pressure and modest Atlantic air advection typical of late autumn. Daytime heating remains limited by seasonal cooling, with average May highs around 22–23 °C and only modest day-to-day variability from passing weak fronts. Model spread in boundary-layer mixing and cloud cover creates the tight clustering of market-implied odds around 22–24 °C, while lower-probability tails reflect the small chance of stronger onshore flow or clearer skies pushing the reading outside that band. Updated model runs and official INMET briefings through May 30 will refine the exact peak before resolution.
